restatement: Inside a markdown TABLE rendered by the template resolver, cell content that contains a pipe or a newline must not break the table. A pipe must come out as \| so the row keeps its column count, and a newline (LF or CRLF) must become a single space. This applies to header cells, static ROW cells and ROW cells generated by FOR. Nothing outside table cells may change, no existing test may be edited or deleted, and no runtime dependency may be added. This serves the cycle goal of fixing the Tier 0 bugs in a deterministic, no-eval template core.
verification_plan: c1: check that a pipe in substituted cell content is emitted as \| in a static ROW, so the rendered row has the same number of unescaped delimiters as columns, including a cell with several pipes and a table with a HEADER.
c2: check that LF and CRLF inside a cell each become exactly one space, and that a cell holding both a pipe and a newline gets both treatments.
c3: check that the same escaping runs for HEADER cells and for ROW cells produced inside a FOR loop. That means the fix sits on a path shared by all three, not on only one of them.

m1: check that values outside a TABLE are untouched, that plain cells render byte-for-byte as before, and that content which is already a valid escape (for example escape_md output) is not changed in a way that breaks the row.
m1: check that the escaping is correct for any backslash run before a pipe, not only for the single-backslash case.
m2: check that no file present at base under tests/ is modified or deleted in the diff.
m3: check that package.json and the lockfile are unchanged and no new import appears.
Goal-critical: check that each frozen test fails before the fix (pipe left raw, newline left raw) and passes after, and that the guard tests pass both before and after.
Scope: check that only nodes/TemplateResolver/interpreter.ts is edited, and that any other path has an approved scope exception.

findings.title: The single-backslash lookbehind leaves a pipe unescaped when an even number of backslashes precedes it, which splits the row

serves.scenario: The new lookbehind (?<!\\)\| skips any pipe that has a backslash directly before it. That is correct for an odd-length backslash run, such as escape_md output or raw '\|'. It is wrong for an even-length run: in raw data like 'x\\|y' (two literal backslashes, then a pipe), GFM reads the two backslashes as one escaped backslash. The pipe then stays a live delimiter, so the row gains a column, which breaks c1. The rule should be: escape a pipe when the backslash run before it has even length, zero included.

findings.rubric: each criterion is met by the diff and its test (c1: a pipe inside a cell is escaped so the row keeps its column count)
findings.reproduction: resolveTemplate('{{TABLE}}{{ROW}}${{a}}|z{{END_ROW}}{{END_TABLE}}', new Map([['a', 'x\\\\|y']]), {strictMode:false}). The JS value is the characters x, \, \, |, y. The output is '| x\\|y | z |' with the pipe left unescaped, because the character before it is a backslash. Under GFM the cell scanner consumes '\\' as one escaped character, so the '|' that follows ends the cell. The row renders as three cells ('x\', 'y', 'z') instead of two. The smallest fix is to escape based on the parity of the backslash run, for example content.replace(/\r?\n/g, ' ').replace(/(\\*)\|/g, (m, b) => b.length % 2 ? m : b + '\\|').trim(). This keeps escape_md output, which always has an odd run before '|', unchanged and still escapes the case above.
evidence: test:table cell escaping with filters > a pipe already escaped by escape_md is not escaped again
